title: postfix ! before an element access compiles and runs: element access was never the distinction
notes: RETIRED REFUSAL, kept under its old filename so the COVERAGE.md row that cites it (§4.14) keeps resolving. specification/failures.mdx §Refusal Conditions withdrew the placement walk; see DECISIONS.md §Typed failures. WHY IT NOW PASSES: `lookup("ada")!` is unconditional, once-evaluated, and has nothing effectful to its left, so its guard hoists to the front of the `const` and the emitted program evaluates `lookup`, checks, then indexes — the authored order. The old rule's distinction between a property access (admitted) and an element access (refused) was a property of its allow-list of seven node kinds and not of evaluation order, which is why it disappears rather than moving. The boundary approached from the other side is unchanged and still pinned elsewhere: specification/compatibility.mdx §Reinterpreted Syntax's `arr[i]!` is `!` APPLIED TO an element read, certified by 07-must-consume/an-array-literal-of-results-is-consumed-through-an-index-read.

xfail.reason: the fork still enforces the withdrawn statement-walk and refuses this program with SMITHERS1204 at the same authored position the retired expectation named. That is a FAIL-CLOSED divergence: the fork compiles nothing and runs nothing, so no marker here holds a fail-open. The reference moved when specification/failures.mdx §Refusal Conditions withdrew the placement rule (DECISIONS.md §Typed failures, 2026-08-30); `safeUnwrapPlacement` in compiler/forkbridge/lowering.go.txt is the fork's copy of the walk and has not been widened yet. The marker retires when the fork's placement walk is narrowed to the three residual conditions the reference now applies: a conditionally evaluated operand, a repeated loop header, and a propagation preceded by an unhoisted effect in the same statement.
